fields.Short Description: Guided boat tours out of Georgetown, narrated by a captain and a naturalist with history, wildlife and local legends. The Lighthouse Shell Island Tour lands on a barrier island reachable only by boat, the Plantation River Tour passes old rice plantations and moss-draped oaks, and sunset eco cruises and private charters are offered. Call to confirm the departure dock.
fields.Hours Note: Book online. In summer, book about two weeks ahead. Tours leave from 701 Front St, Georgetown.
fields.Name: Cap'n Rod's Lowcountry Tours

fields.Short Description: Boat tours from the Georgetown harbor. Address needs confirming.
fields.Name: Rover Boat Tours

fields.Short Description: A historic lowcountry rice plantation house open for tours. The circa-1740 house is seen on a guided tour of about 50 minutes that covers the lives of both the owners and the enslaved people who lived and worked there. Tours run on the hour Tuesday through Saturday, and online booking is available. The riverside grounds overlook the North Santee River.
fields.Hours Note: House tours on the hour. Tours are for ages 6 and up.
fields.Name: Hopsewee Plantation

fields.Short Description: Maritime history on the Georgetown waterfront, with free admission. Exhibits cover South Carolina's maritime past, including a Fresnel lens from the old North Island lighthouse and bricks salvaged from the c. 1730 Brown's Ferry Vessel, along with changing displays and a gift shop. Open Monday through Saturday.
fields.Name: South Carolina Maritime Museum

fields.Short Description: The Franklin G. Burroughs-Simeon B. Chapin Art Museum is Myrtle Beach's only art museum, on South Ocean Boulevard across from the beach. Eleven galleries show rotating exhibitions of paintings, textiles, sculpture, photography, video, ceramics and collage. The museum also hosts artist receptions, tours, lectures, and workshops and classes for adults and children.
fields.Address: 3100 S Ocean Blvd, Myrtle Beach, SC 29577
fields.Name: Myrtle Beach Art Museum

fields.Short Description: Exhibits on nearly 300 years of local history, from colonial beginnings and the Revolutionary era to the indigo, rice, lumber and paper industries and today's tourism economy. The museum also houses the Francis Marion Interpretive Center and has a gift shop. The building has an entrance ramp and an elevator to the second floor. Free admission.
fields.Name: Georgetown County Museum

fields.Short Description: The Horry County Museum in Conway tells the history, prehistory and natural history of Horry County through local exhibits and a custom-built freshwater aquarium of area rivers and lakes that was featured on Animal Planet's Tanked. It is housed in the renovated 1905 Burroughs School, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, which the museum moved into in 2014. Admission is free. The museum was founded in 1979, opened to the public in 1981, and also runs the L.W. Paul Living History Farm.
fields.Name: Horry County Museum

fields.Short Description: The Moorish-style winter home of Archer and Anna Hyatt Huntington, inside Huntington Beach State Park. Visitors can explore the castle for a small separate fee on top of park entry. Pair it with the beach, birding and the freshwater lake in the same park.
fields.Hours Note: Open until 5 PM during Daylight Saving Time. May close for large events.
fields.Price: $2 per person ages 6+, plus state park admission ($8 adults, $4 ages 6–15)
fields.Address: Huntington Beach State Park, 16148 Ocean Hwy, Murrells Inlet, SC 29576
fields.Name: Atalaya Castle

fields.Short Description: A downtown true-crime museum owned by profiler Phil Chalmers and billed as the world's only permanent serial killer museum. The self-guided visit covers four themed areas, profiles of more than 450 killers and over 200 artifacts, with a scavenger hunt included. Plan on about two hours; phones aren't allowed on the museum floor. Aimed at adults.
fields.Hours Note: Open Tuesday too from May to October
fields.Price: General $35; ages 10-12 $20; under 9 free; locals and heroes $30 with ID
fields.Name: Serial Killers: The Experience

fields.Short Description: A museum and education center telling the story of the 1932 school that served the area's Black students for more than two decades, rebuilt in 2006 with help from former students.
fields.Name: Historic Myrtle Beach Colored School Museum

fields.Short Description: A historic house museum on the Sampit River.
fields.Name: Kaminski House Museum

fields.Short Description: Start at the Conway Visitor Center in a historic building on Main Street for a self-guided historic walking tour of downtown Conway, where many sites are listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The center also offers a tree tour and a mural guide, and guided historic tours can be arranged by reservation for individuals and groups.
fields.Hours Note: Visitor Center hours aren't posted online; call ahead for guided tours
fields.Name: Historic Downtown Conway Walking Tour

fields.Short Description: Run by the Horry County Museum, this working farm shows daily life on a Horry County farm family's land between 1900 and 1955. Seasonal demonstrations include a blacksmith shop, gristmill, farm animals, tobacco raising and cane syrup making. Free guided tours of about an hour are offered on Saturday mornings.
fields.Hours Note: Guided tours Saturdays at 10:00 (staff permitting, not on holidays or farm event days); call ahead
fields.Address: 2279 Harris Short Cut Rd, Conway, SC 29526
fields.Name: L.W. Paul Living History Farm

fields.Short Description: The story of Georgetown's rice culture in the old Market Building. The museum also has the Prevost Art Gallery for local art, a shop of local makers' goods, books and culinary items, and occasional workshops such as indigo dyeing. Open Tuesday through Saturday; check the website for current hours.
fields.Name: Rice Museum

fields.Short Description: A vintage auto museum that celebrates the beauty and craftsmanship of cars from earlier eras, including vintage American cars and trucks and the original Charger Daytona from the movie Joe Dirt. Along with the vehicles, visitors browse car-related memorabilia and pop-culture items, including license plates from around the world.
fields.Hours Note: Closed Easter Sunday, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day
fields.Name: Wheels of Yesteryear

fields.Short Description: A lantern-led walk of one to one-and-a-half miles through Georgetown's historic district and harbor, led by a licensed guide in period dress. Stories cover heartbroken lovers, plantation owners, pirates and lost ships. Tours run Friday evenings at dusk by reservation, with at least five adults. Call for the meeting point.
fields.Hours Note: Friday evenings at dusk, by reservation only (at least five adults). Times change with the season.
fields.Name: Ghosts of Georgetown Lantern Tours
